register.name: Climate Resilient, Regenerative Agricultural Systems in Tonga, Vanuatu and Samoa (FP295)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved by the Board 28 March 2026 · funded activity agreement executed 27 August 2026 · grant of USD 42,056,443 for three nations · accredited entity the Pacific Community (SPC) · total value $43.7M
register.note: 270,000 people expected to gain resilience across Samoa, Tonga and Vanuatu; Samoa’s share is not stated
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, implemented by the Pacific Community, that supports smallholder farmers in Samoa, Tonga and Vanuatu to adopt climate-resilient, regenerative farming through training, demonstration farms and a Farmer Support Programme for tools and equipment. It aims at a secure and resilient supply of food crops across the three nations and serves the food standard, where 18.6% of Samoans are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Pacific Region Preparedness, Adaptation and Resilience (PREPARE) – Samoa
register.detail: World Bank · Board approval announced 20 March 2026 · includes a USD 5 million grant from the Systematic Observations Financing Facility · implemented by the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment and the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure
register.note: About 180,000 people, 80% of the population, expected to benefit
register.text: World Bank financing of USD 35 million (about WST 94.89 million) for multi-hazard early warning, more resilient critical infrastructure and risk-informed urban planning, with a significant focus on Sālelologa on Savai’i. It makes the places where Samoans live and work safer from cyclones, floods and tsunamis and finances civil works that create jobs; it serves shelter, the standard furthest from reach, and livelihood.

register.name: Finance Sector Resilience and Development Project
register.detail: World Bank · grant of US$21 million (WST$57.6 million) · approved 18 October 2024 · announced 28 October 2024
register.note: 8,500 people and businesses to use financial services more easily and at lower cost
register.text: A World Bank grant to upgrade Samoa’s national payment systems, set up its first national digital identification system and lower the cost of sending and receiving money from abroad. Remittances equal 22.4% of GDP, so cheaper transfers reach families directly; it serves livelihood.

register.name: Digitally Connected and Resilient Samoa Project
register.detail: World Bank · grant of US$20.05 million · approved 18 October 2024 · announced 3 November 2024
register.note: An estimated 215,000 Samoans expected to benefit
register.text: A World Bank grant to extend climate-resilient fibre-optic networks to underserved communities on Upolu and Savai’i, strengthen the Government’s delivery of digital public services and keep critical government systems running in emergencies. It connects communities to services and to work, and serves livelihood.

register.name: Integrated Flood Management to Enhance Climate Resilience of the Vaisigano River Catchment (FP037)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved 15 December 2016 · accredited entity UNDP · grant of USD 31,572,322.7 · 90% disbursed · under implementation · total value $39.6M
register.note: An older line, still under implementation; about 37,000 people expected to gain resilience
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, implemented with UNDP, for integrated flood management in the Vaisigano River catchment of Apia, which holds schools, hospitals and government buildings as well as private homes and businesses. It protects homes from flooding and serves shelter, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Sun Pacific Solar Expansion Project
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · approved 15 August 2025 · loan 4618 from ordinary capital resources · signed August 2025 · borrower Sun Pacific Energy Limited
register.note: Higher-efficiency panels for a 4.2 megawatt-peak solar farm on Upolu
register.text: An ADB private sector loan to Sun Pacific Energy Limited to expand its 4.2 megawatt-peak solar farm on Upolu by installing higher-efficiency solar panels. It contributes to Samoa’s goal of 70% renewable energy use by 2031 and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Alaoa Multipurpose Dam Project
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · approved 12 June 2024 · grant of $99.7M from the Asian Development Fund · $400,000 from the Ireland Trust Fund · more than $11M from the Government of Samoa · total project $111M
register.note: A dam with 3 million cubic metres of reservoir storage in Apia
register.text: An ADB grant for a multipurpose dam to reduce flood risk in Apia and provide a reliable and sustainable source of water supply, with a run-of-river small hydropower plant that will help to reduce Samoa’s dependency on imported fossil fuels. It serves water, where 62.5% of Samoans have safely managed drinking water, and energy.

register.name: Economic and Social Development Programme: Provision of Medical Equipment
register.detail: Government of Japan · grant aid · Exchange of Notes signed 27 October 2026 · JPY 470 million (about SAT 8.25 million)
register.note: Equipment for emergency, surgical, laboratory and maternal care, focused on Tupua Tamasese Meaole Hospital
register.text: Japanese grant aid for medical equipment for emergency care, surgery, laboratory testing and maternal health care, replacing ageing devices at Tupua Tamasese Meaole Hospital on Upolu, a hospital on Savai’i and district hospitals. It contributes to efforts towards Universal Health Coverage and serves the health standard, where Samoa scores 62 on the WHO service coverage index.

register.name: Economic and Social Development Programme: Equipment for the Development of Underground Water Resources
register.detail: Government of Japan · grant aid · Exchange of Notes signed in Apia 5 December 2024 · up to JPY 390 million · equipment for the Samoa Water Authority
register.note: Groundwater equipment for the Samoa Water Authority
register.text: Japanese grant aid of up to 390 million yen for equipment to develop underground water resources, provided to the Samoa Water Authority to secure drinking water and water for daily life. It serves the water standard, where 62.5% of Samoans have safely managed drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 38.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Women in Business Development Inc (WIBDI)
items.text: A Samoan organisation that promotes organic farming and buys virgin coconut oil made by women in rural villages, most of it sold to The Body Shop in the United Kingdom, to increase cash income for women in rural areas.

items.name: SPBD Samoa (South Pacific Business Development)
items.text: A microfinance institution, established in Samoa in 2000, that offers credit, savings and business skills training to women micro-entrepreneurs, with over 118,400 loans disbursed in Samoa since inception, worth US$103 million.
